title: Logging, monitoring, detection and incident response
subtitle: Make useful records, validate alerts, preserve evidence and coordinate recovery.
description: Make useful records, validate alerts, preserve evidence and coordinate recovery. Guided explanations, six original visual diagrams, safe practice, trusted resource links, worked examples and a randomized quiz.

blocks.text: Lesson 7 — Logging, monitoring, detection and incident response

LEARNING OUTCOME
Make useful records, validate alerts, preserve evidence and coordinate recovery.

Safety rule: work only with devices, accounts and training applications you own or have explicit written permission to assess. Use synthetic information. A public system or a suspicious person is not permission.

Useful logs help show what happened, when, to which asset and through which identity. Collect sign-in events, permission changes, administrative actions, security alerts and key application errors. Use consistent timestamps and protect logs from tampering. Avoid logging raw passwords, tokens, sensitive request bodies or unnecessary personal data.

blocks.text: An alert is a signal to investigate. Validate data sources, asset identity, time window and business context; correlate sources before making a conclusion. Rate urgency based on impact, scope, active exposure and confidence, and document the reasoning for the next analyst.

blocks.text: Define who can declare an incident, isolate a system, preserve evidence, contact leadership and approve recovery. Containment should be coordinated; hasty deletion can destroy evidence or interrupt services. After recovery, find the root cause, close weaknesses, and update controls and playbooks.

blocks.text: Practice checklist: (1) read the lab rules, (2) use fabricated data or an isolated training target, (3) predict what the control should do, (4) test one small condition, (5) save only minimal evidence, and (6) explain the defensive follow-up. Stop and ask the owner if any target or action is outside the approved scope.

blocks.output: Use synthetic events and redact tokens or private details.

blocks.question: Which detail should generally be excluded from application logs?
blocks.explanation: Secrets in logs can turn monitoring systems into a source of exposure.

blocks.question: What does an alert mean?
options: Proof that one named person attacked the system
A signal that needs validation and triage
blocks.explanation: Validate the source, context and evidence before concluding what happened.

blocks.question: Which approach better protects private information?
options: Use synthetic data and collect only necessary, authorized evidence
Copy all customer records for convenience
blocks.explanation: Data minimization and redaction reduce privacy and exposure risks.

blocks.question: What is a sound step after applying a fix?

blocks.explanation: Retesting verifies the correction and preserves a useful record.
